name: DC transfer characterization of commercial 5 nm n/p-FinFETs from 300 K down to 10 K on a closed-cycle cryogenic probe station
plain_name: Measure how the tiniest commercial transistors behave when cooled to 10 K
description: Ids-Vgs transfer curves (Vds 50 mV and 750 mV) of minimum-length multi-fin 5 nm FinFETs probed directly on their gate, source, drain and bulk pads in a Lake Shore CRX-VF closed-cycle cryogenic probe station from 300 K to 10 K with a Keysight B1500A; the data calibrate a cryogenic-aware BSIM-CMG compact model.
keywords: Measure how the tiniest commercial transistors behave when cooled to 10 K

sources.citation: Design Automation for Cryogenic CMOS Circuits (van Santen et al., DAC 2023, doi:10.1109/DAC56929.2023.10247824)

requirements.rationale: Transistors were measured over the whole span from 300 K down to 10 K (10 K was the lowest stable temperature with probes landed).
The probed die sits in the evacuated sample space of the probe station.
Each transistor terminal (gate, source, drain, bulk) is contacted by its own probe, so four probe arms are needed.
The DUT is biased and measured by the B1500A through the probes.
Optional: the source used a two-stage closed-cycle refrigerator rather than a liquid cryogen.

confirmation_note: Requirements taken from the cited procedure and independently re-verified against the source (research/v4, 2026-11-01). Users must confirm them for their own run; edits require confirmation again.
